title: Shared-phreatic process and internal-memory decomposition
activation_rule: Execute only after HLINK01 and HLINK02 have both passed their preregistered live gates.
basis: GC-DUMMY-SWAP-DSW11 shared head with independent memory

memory_law.ownership: T is internal transfer: +T to shared phreatic storage and -T in SWAP memory; it is not an external whole-system source.

modflow_mapping.sto_role: owns the one shared phreatic storage response exactly once
modflow_mapping.api_role: SWAP process remainder only: atmospheric input + internal memory transfer - ET(H) - drain(H)

gates: Both cases use the same initial shared head, same shared storage ownership and same external forcing except internal memory W0.
DRY_MEMORY ends at 8.06 m within 1e-10 m and closes whole-system mass within 1e-12 m.
WET_MEMORY ends at 8.074285714285714 m within 1e-10 m and closes whole-system mass within 1e-12 m.
The wet-memory case transfers exactly 0.005 m internally; this transfer appears with opposite signs in shared storage and memory ledgers.
ET and drain are reconstructed independently from the accepted shared head and match the analytical amounts.
The different final heads prove that H_phreatic alone is not a complete SWAP state even in a valid shared-phreatic storage contract.
adversarial_followup_not_in_primary_gate: A later control may deliberately count the memory transfer as an external source without reducing W to demonstrate whole-system mass creation; do not add that control before this primary decomposition passes.
forbidden: do not execute before HLINK02 passes
do not count internal memory transfer as external recharge
do not infer these linear ET/drain laws are production SWAP process formulations
do not infer shared head is sufficient to reconstruct SWAP internal state
